name: Institute for Biodiversity and Protected Areas
territory_ids: bijagos-archipelago; orango-national-park; joao-vieira-poilao; urok-community-mpa; cacheu-region; cacheu-mangroves-park
role: Created in 2004 to protect and manage Guinea-Bissau's biodiversity through the National System of Protected Areas, which covers about 26% of the national territory. It coordinates management of the Bijagós World Heritage property and manages the Cacheu park. Its 2006 annual report records the appointment of wardens for the Orango, João Vieira–Poilão and Cacheu parks; current park-level arrangements were not re-verified.

name: BioGuinea Foundation
role: Conservation trust fund established in 2011 as a long-term financing mechanism for Guinea-Bissau's protected areas, with funding channelled through IBAP. It supports Orango National Park, runs the Blue Bijagós project and runs a community REDD+ project in the Cacheu and Cantanhez parks. It is listed as a member of the Consortium of African Funds for the Environment (CAFÉ).
role_source_ids: gef-bioguinea-2011; bioguinea-about; bioguinea-bijagos; bioguinea-blue-bijagos; fbg-annual-report-2025; cafe-members

name: Tiniguena – Esta Terra é Nossa
role: Guinean NGO that supported the creation and participatory governance of the Urok Islands Community Marine Protected Area.

name: Wetlands International (West Africa)
role: With IBAP and partners, ran a 2015–2018 initiative to conserve and restore the Cacheu mangroves, including ecological restoration of abandoned rice fields, solar salt and a fuel-efficient fish-smoking oven. It reports that its support has improved the conservation status of 82,000 hectares of mangroves across the Cacheu and Cantanhez parks. In Liberia's Lake Piso reserve it has supported improved stoves and a cassava processing unit under an EU-funded mangrove project.

name: International Union for Conservation of Nature
role: Provided technical assistance to the coastal planning that led to the 1996 Bolama-Bijagós Biosphere Reserve.

name: The Restoration Initiative
role: Restoration programme uniting 10 countries and three Global Environment Facility agencies (IUCN, FAO and UNEP). Its Guinea-Bissau project works with women on Elia Island, near the mouth of the Cacheu River. The reviewed source does not say which agency leads the Guinea-Bissau project.

name: Regional Partnership for Coastal and Marine Conservation in West Africa
role: Regional coalition for the conservation and sustainable management of West Africa's coastal and marine areas. It partners with Rainforest Trust on a proposed project supporting new marine protected area designations in the Bijagós.

name: Rainforest Trust
role: Raising funds, with PRCM, to support government designation of four new marine protected areas in the Bijagós, including three island community MPAs (proposed project).

name: Acção para o Desenvolvimento
role: National NGO supporting a network of environmental schools (EVA) around the park.

name: CE3C – Centre for Ecology, Evolution and Environmental Changes (University of Lisbon)
role: Runs a research project on the ecological integrity of the Bijagós as a key site for waders on the East Atlantic Flyway, with partners including Tiniguena.

name: Centre National de Gestion des Réserves de Faune
role: Benin's national wildlife-reserve agency; supervising administration of the Bouche du Roy marine protected area inside the reserve.

name: Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit
role: Implemented the 2013–2019 project, funded by the German International Climate Initiative, that prepared the transboundary biosphere reserve.

name: IUCN National Committee of the Netherlands
role: Worked with local partners, GIZ and both governments to create the reserve, and partners Eco-Benin on blue-carbon mangrove work.

name: Eco-Benin
role: Beninese NGO running mangrove restoration and sacralisation and a blue-carbon project in the Bouche du Roy area of the reserve.

name: Hydrocarbon Pollution Remediation Project
role: Federal agency under the Ministry of Environment carrying out the Ogoniland clean-up, mangrove restoration and livelihood programmes, and preparing the Ramsar site management plan.

name: United Nations Environment Programme
role: Carried out the 2011 independent environmental assessment of Ogoniland whose recommendations frame the clean-up.

name: Fundação Maio Biodiversidade
role: Maio NGO that managed the Salinas under a 2012 delegation, monitors its birds and turtles, and leads co-management of Maio's protected areas.

name: Direção Nacional do Ambiente (Cabo Verde)
role: National environment directorate with the mandate and authority on biodiversity and conservation in Cabo Verde.

name: Office Ivoirien des Parcs et Réserves
role: Holds delegated management of the national-park part of the Ramsar site.

name: West Africa Coastal Areas Management Program (WACA)
role: World Bank-financed coastal resilience programme; funded mangrove restoration with OIPR in Côte d'Ivoire and mangrove planting in Togo.

name: Wildlife Division, Forestry Commission of Ghana
role: Management authority of the Keta Lagoon Complex Ramsar Site, mandated to enforce the law.

name: A Rocha Ghana
role: Ran the 2021–2023 PAPBio mangrove restoration and livelihoods project in four Keta Lagoon communities, with the Wildlife Division.

name: Ministère de l'Environnement (Togo)
role: Its staff act against unsustainable logging, fishing and illegal hunting at the site; it is the implementing agency of WACA in Togo.

name: Climate Technology Centre and Network
role: UNFCCC technology body that prepared a 2025 technical-assistance plan for women-led mangrove restoration and solar fish preservation in Togo's Maritime Region.

name: Parc National du Banc d'Arguin
role: Public administrative body that manages the park under its own law (2000-024).

name: BACoMaB Trust Fund (Fonds Fiduciaire du Banc d'Arguin et de la Biodiversité Côtière et Marine)
role: Conservation trust fund created in 2009 that provides long-term funding for the park, including sea surveillance and shared governance.

name: Direction des Parcs Nationaux (Senegal)
role: Named as the park's managing body in the 1993 Ramsar sheet; UNESCO names it as a partner in integrated management planning.

name: Océanium
role: Senegalese marine conservation association that proposed and led the Bamboung community marine protected area project.

name: TRY Oyster Women's Association
role: Community-based non-profit founded in 2007 that holds exclusive cockle and oyster use rights in Tanbi; it received the Equator Prize in 2012.

name: Department of Parks and Wildlife Management (The Gambia)
role: Has managed the Tanbi Wetlands Complex since 2005 and assists with enforcement under the shellfish co-management plan.

name: Coastal Resources Center, University of Rhode Island
role: Implemented the USAID Ba Nafaa project, with WWF, that supported the Tanbi shellfish co-management plan.

name: Guinée Écologie
role: Guinean NGO running mangrove restoration, solar salt, improved ovens and oyster pilots in the Konkouré delta, and a partner in the PROMAK protected-area project.

name: GRET
role: Leads the EU-funded PROMAK consortium (2025–2028) working towards legal protection of the Konkouré mangroves.

name: Office Guinéen des Parcs Nationaux et Réserves de Faune
role: Named as the future manager of the protected area proposed for the Konkouré mangroves.

name: National Protected Area Authority (Sierra Leone)
role: Statutory protected-area authority; carries out enforcement against encroachment at the estuary, though its mandate over wetlands is limited.

name: Freetown City Council
role: Runs mangrove planting in Freetown coastal communities under its #FreetownTheTreeTown campaign.

name: Sierra Leone Nature Guide Association
role: Ran bird-conservation and nature-guiding training around the Targreen wetland in 2024.

name: Forestry Development Authority (Liberia)
role: National authority for conservation forestry; lists the Lake Piso Multiple Sustainable Use Reserve among Liberia's protected areas.

name: Environmental Protection Agency of Liberia
role: Named in the 2007 Ramsar sheet as the agency responsible for the Lake Piso wetland.

name: Women United for Development
role: Grantee of a 2016–2017 GEF small-grant project on sustainable fishing at Lake Piso.
